answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during settlement peak, 90 minutes into a climb that began after a release. That regional confinement matches the March latency case more closely than a global bad-build signature, so the current best single move is a guarded regional failover that keeps customer writes flowing on a healthy region. Rollback historically cleared an error spike, not a latency-only write-path stall, and mid-peak capacity add was not how headroom previously worked (it was provisioned before the surge). Circuit breaking would drop writes; replica routing addressed reporting reads, not settlement writes. Uncertain whether the release was primary-only canary-scoped and whether failover under peak write weight has unstated caveats, so verify b2 and b1 before committing and keep the shift small. Downstream settlement value is at risk if the secondary absorbs the full write peak untested.
